entities.summary:
Asclepigenia (d. 485 CE) was a pivotal Athenian Neoplatonist philosopher and mystic, renowned for her profound mastery and transmission of the Chaldean Oracles and the teachings of Plato and Aristotle. Active in 5th-century CE Athens, she represents a crucial link in the late antique pagan intellectual tradition, bridging the philosophical insights of her father, Plutarch of Athens, and her student, Proclus. Her work sustained the Academy's syncretic curriculum amidst growing Christian hegemony, making her a formidable intellectual force in the twilight of classical paganism.

Born into the intellectual elite of Athens, Asclepigenia received an unparalleled education, first from her father, Plutarch, who initiated her into the esoteric doctrines of the Chaldean Oracles, believed to confer theurgic powers. Following Plutarch's death, she continued her studies under Syrianus, the next head of the Athenian Neoplatonic Academy, whose extensive commentaries on Plato and Aristotle further shaped her rigorous philosophical approach. She, in turn, became the primary instructor for Proclus, widely considered the last great classical philosopher, imparting to him not only the systematic Neoplatonic curriculum but also the unique, almost sacramental knowledge of the Oracles, which she was said to transmit directly.
